analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: one added table row at head line 1960, documenting DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS (read by SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpoints; a negative value writes complete checkpoints instead of deltas). No executable code, auth, attestation or crypto logic changes. I read the full base units (6, 7) and the first portion of the head unit (8). The head unit only covers lines 1-396, so the added row at ~1960 is visible only via the patch excerpt and not as a numbered line.

Threat-model relevance: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, KVCacheSSD) and SEC-035. The row names a new environment knob for SSD cache checkpoint encoding (delta vs complete). Whether incremental checkpoints alter the DBK3 on-disk format, metadata/AAD, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, or per-donation gating cannot be determined from the doc change. T-041's detection_hint says nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to DBK3 metadata, and that loosening donation gating widens the at-rest surface. The accompanying code change in SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift and the SSD block store is not supplied, so this contract is unverified. The docs row indicates the knob only selects the checkpoint encoding and does not claim to change the crypto or retention. The variable is not listed as forwarded into the LaunchAgent (the doc says other variables reach the engine only under foreground/local), so no new daemon environment passthrough is implied by this change.

No concrete regression is supported by the supplied evidence. Follow-up for any pass that sees the code: confirm that delta checkpoints keep nothing prompt-derived on disk besides HMAC tags, retain AAD binding per chain/salt scope, and that reconstruction of deltas fails closed on a missing or tampered parent. Also confirm the TTL and LRU sweep covers delta chains without leaving orphaned ciphertext.
